facts.statement: Ondogurvel is a genus of alvarezsaurid dinosaur known from the Late Cretaceous Barun Goyot Formation in southern Mongolia.
facts.quote: Ondogurvel (meaning "egg lizard") is a genus of alvarezsaurid dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous (Campanian) Barun Goyot Formation in southern Mongolia.

facts.statement: The only known species, O. alifanovi, is known from a partial skeleton including vertebrae, pelvic bones, leg bones, and hand fragments.
facts.quote: The type and only species is O. alifanovi, known from a partial skeleton consisting of fragments of two last dorsal vertebrae, three anterior sacral vertebrae, right ilium, left and right pubis and ischium, articulated right tibia, fibula, metatarsals II and IV, and phalanges IV-1 and IV-2, right carpometacarpus, left and right manual phalanx II-1, right femur, left pedal phalanx II-1, and fragments of unidentified phalanges.

facts.statement: The species was named and described in 2022 by Alexander O. Averianov and Alexey V. Lopatin.
facts.quote: In 2022, the type species Ondogurvel alifanovi was named and described by Alexander O. Averianov and Alexey V. Lopatin.

facts.statement: The specific name honors Vladimir Alifanov, who discovered the holotype specimen in 1999.
facts.quote: The specific name, "alifanovi" honors the late Russian paleontologist Vladimir Alifanov who found the holotype specimen (PIN 5838/1) in 1999.

facts.statement: Ondogurvel was a bipedal theropod dinosaur.
Some researchers suggest that Ondogurvel might be a junior synonym of Parvicursor, though this is debated.
facts.quote: Mickey Mortimer has suggested that Ondogurvel may be a junior synonym of Parvicursor, which is known only from a juvenile individual.

facts.statement: Ondogurvel is classified within the alvarezsaurid subfamily Parvicursorinae based on hand morphology.
facts.quote: Averianov and Lopatin (2022) place Ondogurvel in the alvarezsaurid subfamily Parvicursorinae which are classified by their manus morphology.

facts.statement: Ondogurvel lived during the Campanian stage of the Late Cretaceous, between 83.6 and 72.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: Ondogurvel belongs to the family Alvarezsauridae.
It lived at the end of the Cretaceous period, approximately 72 million years ago, in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 72 millones de años en el Campaniense, en lo que hoy es Asia.

rejected.quote: Like other parvicursorines, it had a robust humerus, and long hindlimbs suggesting a cusorial lifestyle.
